rounds.why_not_controlling: Superseded by round 2. A verdict bound to a head that has since moved cannot govern the later head, and the phase gate requires MUST_FIX 0. Retained verbatim as the controlling evidence for why the repair exists.

auditor_wrote_one_file_in_its_throwaway_.what_happened: In round 2 the auditor wrote its report to proof/TP-DMX-SECOND-BRAIN-ADR-ACCEPTANCE-002/AUDITOR_REPORT.md inside its own throwaway checkout, overwriting round 1's report there.
auditor_wrote_one_file_in_its_throwaway_.scope: The throwaway worktree only. git status in that worktree showed exactly one modified tracked file and one untracked hook cache.
auditor_wrote_one_file_in_its_throwaway_.impact_on_evidence: None. The producer branch was never written to by the auditor, and the committed round-1 report was re-hashed after the run and is byte-identical to what was committed (9f9063858cae345a3fe8ad8f631b505cb9e4eb70d50d8dc6bc261eb08c54805c).
auditor_wrote_one_file_in_its_throwaway_.how_it_was_handled: The round-2 report was taken from that file and committed under a DISTINCT filename, AUDITOR_REPAIR_REPORT.md, so no round's report overwrites another. The throwaway worktree was discarded.
auditor_wrote_one_file_in_its_throwaway_.recorded_because: An audit that was asked to be read-only performed one write. It changed nothing, but a reader should learn that from the record rather than discover it.

residual_risks: Auditor identity rests on the runner's own session store, not on provider-side cryptographic attestation. Same residual this route has carried since PR #1214.
Round 2 read round 1's report as part of its input. It was instructed to treat those findings as prior claims to recheck rather than as fact, and it recomputed them, but it was not a blind re-audit.
